full_judgment:
2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus that the present opposite party No. 1 as pre-emptor instituted the original pre-emption Miscellaneous Case under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act, 1949 against the pre-emptee-opposite party and others contending inter alia that the case land appertaining to RS Khatian No.159 originally belonged to one Solim Uddin Pramanik and others. The father of the pre-emptor namely Najibor Rahman was one of the RS recorded tenant and the pre-emptor's father on 19-1-1967 AD by way of a kabala deed No.450 and on 20-1-1968 AD by dint of another kabala deed No.760 purchased 11½ decimals of land from the opposite party No. 4 and the predecessor of the opposite parties No. 5-8, Noimuddin and father of the opposite party No. 9 and 10, Najimuddin. After that purchase the purchaser erected homestead in the purchased land. After his demise the wife Rashida Bewa, two sons the pre-emptor-petitioner and the opposite party No. 2 and one daughter the opposite party No. 3 became the heirs. After the death of Nojibor Rahman his heirs mutated the land jointly and holding No. 360 was opined in their names. They paid rent to the Government and obtained rent receipts. Subsequently; Rashida Bewa died leaving behind her two sons and one daughter the pre-emptor-petitioner and the opposite party No. 2 and 3. In this way; the pre-emptor-petitioner with other co-sharers possess the case jote which is a homestead. They are in ejmali possession in the case jote and one of the co-sharer of the pre-emptor the pro-forma opposite party No. 2 Md Shohrab Morshed behind the back of the pre-emptor-petitioner on 16-1-2005 transferred the case land in favour of a stranger-purchaser opposite party No. 1 without serving any notice to other co-sharers. The case kabala was executed and registered behind the back of the pre-emptor-petitioner and, as such, he was in the dark about the transfer. The further case of the pre-emptor-petitioner is such that the purchaser-opposite party No.1 who is the pre-emptee to the original case was a monthly tenant in the case land for a long term. On 10-8-2005 the pre-emptor-petitioner coming to his homestead from his place of service, Rajshahi came to know from the people of the locality that the case land has been transferred by the opposite party No. 2 in favour of the opposite party No.1. Thereafter; the pre-emptor-petitioner obtained certified copy of the case kabala on 15-8-2005 and finally came to learn about the case kabala in favour of the pre-emptee-opposite party No.1 which was registered on 4-5-2005 AD. The pre-emptor-petitioner for his urgent need thereafter instituted the original pre-emption Miscellaneous Case being No. 84 of 2005 in the Court of learned Senior Assistant Judge, Naogaon, Sadar, for getting the case land pre-empted , under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act, 1949. 

 9. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party opposing the Rule controverted the arguments advanced from the side of the petitioner and submits that, neither the trial court nor the lower appellate court during disposal of the original case and its subsequent appeal committed any sort of illegality or irregularity. The learned Advocate further submits that the original case was not barred by the principle of estoppel, waiver and acquiescence and the joma was not separated individually, rather; it was a joint holding in the name of the heirs of admitted owner Nojibor Rahman and as because; the holding was in the names of all co-sharers, the payment of rent was jointly in respect of the case property. The learned Advocate further submits that during disposal of the appeal there was no misreading or non-reading of evidence or non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice by which the impugned judgment and order can be interfered with. The learned Advocate during his argument argued that admittedly the case property is a homestead which is under possession Of the heirs of Nojibor Rahman and it is also an admitted position that in a dwelling hut situated in the case jote, the pre-emptee-purchaser-opposite party No.1 was a monthly tenant under one of the co-sharer of the joint holding i.e. the proforma opposite party No.2 who is the vendor of the case kabala. The learned Advocate in his submission submits that, practically only on two grounds this revisional application was filed and those are on the ground of limitation and On the ground of defect of party and both the two grounds were conclusively decided by the courts below in their judgment and orders on the basis of evidence led from the sides of the respective parties. The learned Advocate submits that the pleading's case of the pre-emptee-opposite party to the original case is not at all proved by any authentic paper or evidence and there is no evidence that the case was barred by the principle of estoppel, waiver and acquiescence. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the case laws cited and given from the side of the learned counsel for the petitioner has no manner of application in the instant case, inasmuch as; the facts and circumstances of this case is quite different and due to its distinguishable character, those decisions have no nexus in this case. In this context; the learned Advocate has pointed out Exhibit-6 which is the proposed khatian after mutation on which the pre-emptee-petitioner banks upon. Besides this; Exhibit 6(Ka) which is the DCR and Exhibit-6(Kha) which is rent receipt go to show that the joma was not separated among the brothers and sisters i.e. the heirs of Nojibor Rahman the admitted owner of the case property. The learned Advocate argued that sub-section (2) of section 24 of the Non Agricultural Tenancy Act, 1949 is also not applicable in this case, since; the pre-emptor is the petitioner who claimed the case land by way of pre-emption from the pre-emptee who is the purchaser i.e. the vendee of the case kabala. In support of the contention the learned Advocate referred some decisions reported in 27 BLT (AD) 75, 50 DLR 147, 54 DLR 285, 52 DLR 609 and 35 DLR (AD) 230. 

 10. Considering the submissions of the learned Advocate having gone through the case records along with the evidence led from the sides of the respective parties and the documentary evidences produced in support of the cases of the parties it transpires that admittedly the case property originally belonged to Nojibor Rahman, the father of the pre-emptor and the relevant R.S. khatian No.159 which has been marked as Exhibit-1 makes it clear that Najibor Rahman was the recorded tenant. After the death of Najibor Rahman the case jote devolved upon the heirs of Najibor Rahman and the pre-emptor-petitioner along with his brothers and sisters inherited the property left behind their father. It is also apparent from the face of the papers that after the death of Najibor Rahman there has been a separate holding of the case property being No. 360 arising out of a Mutation Case being No. 675/89-90. Two sons and one daughter after the death of Rashida Bewa who was the wife of Najibor Rahman were the legal heirs and the holding was in their names in respect of the property comprising an area of 111/2 decimals. 

 11. On perusal of the case connected papers it further appears that there has been payment of rent in respect of the said property from the side of all the heirs of Najibor Rahman and the proposed khatian was prepared in the names of the sons and daughter of Najibor Rahman after the mutation (vide Exhibit-6), pursuant to which the payment of rent was done followed by DCR marked as Exhibit-6(ka) and rent receipt marked as Exhibit-6(Kha). All these documents apparently shows that in fact; among the co-sharers i.e. the heirs of Nojibor Rahman the joma was not separated and there was a joint holding and all the heirs jointly paid rent and obtained rent receipts from the government. 

 13. PW 1 is the pre-emptor-petitioner to the original case. This witness in support of his pleading testified and in his deposition he has categorically mentioned that his father Nojibor Rahman died leaving behind wife Rashida Bewa, two sons the pre-emptor himself and the vendor-opposite party No. 2 Shohrab Morshed and one daughter the opposite party No. 3 Nasrina Akter. It was testified by the pre-emptor supported by documentary evidence that after the death of their father in respect of 111/2 decimals of land which is the case property there has been a mutation proceeding being No.675/89-90 and a holding was opened jointly in their names which is 360. Pursuant to that holding they have paid rent, Municipality Tax etc. and possess the property jointly which is a homestead. PW 1 further testifies that the case kabala being No. 697 of 2005 registered under section 60 of the Registration Act on 4-5-2005 and in the case transfer there was no service of notice to the co-sharers. In support of the case, the pre-emptor submitted the relevant RS khatian No. 159 which is Exhibit-1, the certified copy of the case kabala-Exhibit-2, the Chalan No. 57 dated 28-8-2005-Exhibit-3, the certified copy of the kabala No. 450 dated 19-1-1967-Exhibit-4 and the certified copy of the kabala No. 760 dated 20-1-1968-Exhibit-5, the proposed khatian after mutation in their names along with DCR and rent receipts-Exhibits-6, 6(Ka) and 6(Kha).
